**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 11 ("Transition Assistance and Data Return") already satisfies the preferred position in full:

| Playbook element | Document |
|---|---|
| Transition assistance up to 6 months at then-current rates | § 11.1 — six months on Customer's request, at the rates in the **expiring Order Form** (better than preferred, since it locks pricing rather than exposing us to rate increases); includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, migration, and continued service at existing scope/SLAs |
| Return of Customer Data within 30 days in machine-readable format | § 11.2 — thirty days, "complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format," with relationships and metadata; plus an express bar on withholding data over a fee dispute |
| Deletion certified thereafter | § 11.3 — deletion only *after* Customer confirms successful return, legal-retention copies remain protected and purpose-limited, and an authorized officer certifies deletion in writing |

Cross-checks confirmed no clause undercuts this: § 10.1 preserves Customer Data rights and ends access only after the transition period; § 9 contains no immediate-deletion or data-forfeiture trigger; § 15 constrains Vendor's processing; and the § 1.3 definition of Customer Data is appropriately broad (excluding only unlinkable telemetry).

Two points are worth noting as favourable deviations we should preserve if the counterparty proposes edits: the fee-dispute non-withholding sentence in 11.2 and the return-before-deletion sequencing in 11.3.
